steps.title: One client, four people
steps.body: This app holds ONE confidential client. Every request names the person it acts for (acting_as), and the engine answers as that person. Pick Alice, then Charlie, and watch the whole page change.

steps.title: Who the engine thinks you are
steps.body: whoami over acting_as: the user the engine resolved for this request and the roles it carries. Not a superuser, not the app's client — so every guard applies.

steps.title: Rooms are a guard, not a query
steps.body: Everyone runs the same rooms query. Alice gets Croatia and Family, Charlie only Family. The chip says which read guard let you in: administrator, member, or a message you wrote there.

steps.title: Live, and only for the room
steps.body: Send a message as Alice into a room. Open a second tab as Bob (?user=bob): it arrives there live if Bob is a member, never if he is not. Each tab refetches as its own user.

steps.title: Try a change you are not allowed
steps.body: As Bob, open #Croatia and add Charlie. The button is not hidden: the engine refuses with ROW_FORBIDDEN, because only a room's administrators may change its links. As Alice, Croatia's administrator, it works — and the room appears in Charlie's tab, live. Administrators can also delete anyone's message in their room.

steps.title: Same SQL, different numbers
steps.body: This panel is one SQL template for everyone. The engine injects the room and message guards into it, so each user counts only what they may read. Switch user and compare; post a message and the numbers move.

steps.title: The model says unique
steps.body: Press + beside Rooms and open one called Croatia: the engine answers UNIQUE_VIOLATION, category conflict. Room names are unique in the model. Any other name opens a room you administer.

steps.title: Edits and deletes are history
steps.body: Click the clock on a message: its edit timeline is a filter on one attribute of the audit history. Delete one of yours and it reappears below, crossed out — recovered from /history, not from this app.

steps.title: The guards live in the model
steps.body: Chat Room and Chat Message carry every rule you just met: members read, administrators change membership and moderate, authors edit. They ship with the model and apply to any client, this one included.

workspaces.title: The data layer is this file
workspaces.html: This tab is chat.xsql: rooms, messages and the activity SQL. Codegen turned it into the chat.ops.room and chat.ops.message functions the app calls, live versions included. Run one and you get exactly what the page gets.
